title: Perfect maps on an open lift with support
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], let U\subset X be a quasi-compact open, and let T\subset X be a closed subset with X\setminus T quasi-compact. Let E be an object of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] and let \alpha:P\to E|_U be a morphism, where P is a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_U) [def-pc-perfect-complex] supported on T\cap U. Then there are a perfect object R of D(\mathcal O_X) supported on T and a morphism \beta:R\to E such that P is a direct summand of R|_U in D(\mathcal O_U), compatibly with \alpha and \beta|_U.

proof.text: Because X is quasi-compact, choose finitely many affine opens covering X\setminus U and induct on their number. The induction reduces to X=U\cup V with V affine; restriction to the smaller overlaps preserves quasi-compactness and all hypotheses.

On the affine open V, apply the affine support-extension lemma [lem-sc-affine-perfect-support-extension] to P|_{U\cap V} and T\cap V. It gives a perfect Q on V supported on T\cap V and an isomorphism Q|_{U\cap V}\simeq(P\oplus P[1])|_{U\cap V}. Compose this with projection to P|_{U\cap V} and the given map \alpha to obtain a map Q|_{U\cap V}\to E|_{U\cap V}.

Apply the affine perfect-map lifting lemma [lem-sc-affine-perfect-map-lift] on V to replace Q by Q'=Q\otimes^L I, still perfect and supported on T\cap V, so that the map Q'|_{U\cap V}\to E|_{U\cap V} lifts to a morphism Q'\to E|_V.

Let a:P\oplus P[1]\to E|_U be \alpha\circ\mathrm{pr}_P (zero on P[1]). Compose the isomorphism Q|_{U\cap V}\simeq(P\oplus P[1])|_{U\cap V} from Step 2 with the inverse of \beta|_{U\cap V}:Q'|_{U\cap V}\to Q|_{U\cap V} to identify Q'|_{U\cap V} with (P\oplus P[1])|_{U\cap V}; the map \gamma|_V from Step 3 is compatible with a on the overlap by its defining lifting equation. Apply [lem-sc-derived-open-gluing] to these two objects, this transition isomorphism, and the maps a and \gamma. It gives R and \beta:R\to E restricting (up to the gluing isomorphisms) to a and \gamma. Perfectness and support on T are local on U\cup V, so R is perfect and supported on T because P\oplus P[1] and Q' are. The inclusion P\to P\oplus P[1] and projection P\oplus P[1]\to P exhibit P as a direct summand of R|_U, and the definition of a gives the required compatibility with \alpha and \beta|_U.
